reviewedReaderValues.title: Law
components: Methods and Techniques of Legal Research
Introduces doctrinal and empirical legal research.
This illustration selects one of three 5 EC options in law and technology.
The revised curriculum reserves 30 EC for open study, normally in semester five.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Law bachelor studies Dutch, European and international law. Students learn to interpret legislation and judgments, build legal arguments and conduct legal research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first two years and the revised 30 EC elective space are confirmed. This record lists 150 EC. The remaining third-year requirements and final assessment still need confirmation before a full comparison can be assessed.

curriculum.limitation: This record shows 150 EC: 120 EC of named first- and second-year study plus 30 EC of open electives. The revised remaining 30 EC, including the final assessment, are not yet confirmed. The catalogue’s outgoing third-year list does not apply to new entrants.

componentNotes.law-21111004y: Introduces legal concepts, case analysis and the use of legislation and judgments. The first year also requires separate zero-credit tutoring and legal-language activities; these do not add credits to the courses shown.
componentNotes.law-21111026y: Introduces doctrinal interpretation, empirical legal research and practical research skills, building on Foundations of the Law.
componentNotes.law-22112002y: Builds on Introduction to Administrative Law and studies public decisions, enforcement, remedies and relations between government and citizens.
componentNotes.law-22112004y: Develops contract formation, interpretation, performance and termination. Entry requires Introduction to Private Law I or its former 10 EC equivalent.
componentNotes.law-22112006y: Develops substantive criminal liability after Introduction to Criminal Law.
componentNotes.law-22112008y: Develops EU internal-market law after Introduction to European Law.
componentNotes.law-22112010y: Develops liability, remedies and intellectual property. Entry requires Introduction to Private Law I or its former 10 EC equivalent; the course builds on the private-law and obligations sequence.
componentNotes.law-22112012y: Applies criminal-law principles to categories of offences, building on Introduction to Criminal Law and Substantive Criminal Law I.
componentNotes.law-22112014y: Uses economic reasoning to examine how private-law rules affect behaviour and welfare.
componentNotes.law-22112016y: Develops acquisition, loss, enforcement and security rights in property. The revised-curriculum entry requirement is completion of both introductory private-law courses.
componentNotes.law-22112020y: Develops constitutional law after Principles of Constitutional Law, including the influence of European and international law.
componentNotes.law-22112022y: Studies the formation, organisation, governance and liability of businesses. Understanding requires prior foundations in obligations and property law.
componentNotes.law-22112070y: This illustration selects Philosophy of Technology and Law. The other 5 EC choices are Entrepreneurship and Technology, and Technology and Private Law. Only one of the three counts in this slot.
componentNotes.law-y3-elective-space: The revised curriculum provides 30 EC of open study, normally in semester five. Approval is required subject to the exemptions for recognised minors and Leiden course packages. Courses must be of sufficient level and must not overlap compulsory study; Honours courses cannot count. Economics and Business Studies minors are restricted where they overlap the compulsory curriculum. Admission and places remain subject to the relevant rules.
